paragraphs.en: The {memorial} to John Todd's environmental legacy lies in his revolutionary eco-machines.When John Todd was a child, he loved to explore the {woods} around his house, {observing} how nature solved problems.A {dirty} {stream} , for example, often became clear after {flowing} through {plants} and along rocks where {tiny} {creatures} lived.This is where his journey began as a {tale} of scientific exploration.When he got older, John started to wonder if this process could be used to clean up the {messes} people were making.
paragraphs.cn: 约翰·托德在环境方面留下功绩的 <u> 纪念 </u> 体现在他那些具有革命性的生态机器上。在约翰·托德还是个孩子的时候，他就喜欢探索家附近的 <u> 树林 </u> ， <u> 观察 </u> 大自然是如何解决问题的。例如，一条 <u> 污浊的溪流 </u> 在 <u> 流 </u> 经 <u> 植物 </u> 和 <u> 微小生物 </u> 栖息的岩石后，往往会变得清澈起来。这就是他科学探险 <u> 故事 </u> 开始的地方。随着年龄的增长，约翰开始思考这个过程是否可以用来清理人们制造的（环境） <u> 乱象 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: After studying {agriculture} , {medicine} , and {fisheries} in college, John came to the {entrance} of the new field of ecological engineering.He went back to observing nature and asking questions.Why can certain plants trap {harmful} bacteria ( (细菌) )? Which kinds of {fish} can eat cancer-causing {chemicals} ? With the right combination of {animals} and plants, he figured, maybe he could clean up waste the way nature did.He decided to build what he would later call an eco-machine.
paragraphs.cn: 在大学学习了 <u> 农业 </u> 、 <u> 医学 </u> 和 <u> 渔业 </u> 后，约翰进入了生态工程这一新兴领域的 <u> 大门 </u> 。他重新开始观察自然，并提出问题。为什么某些植物能捕获 <u> 有害 </u> 细菌？哪种 <u> 鱼 </u> 能吃掉致癌 <u> 化学物质 </u> ？他想，通过 <u> 动物 </u> 和植物的正确组合，也许他就能像大自然那样净化废物了。他决定制造一种他后来称之为“生态机器”的东西。

paragraphs.en: The task John set for {himself} was to remove harmful {substances} from some sludge ( (污泥) ).First, he {constructed} a simple {format} for organizing a series of clear fiberglass ( (玻璃纤维) ) {tanks} connected to each other.Each tank served as a mini-ecosystem, a {vehicle} for nature's own purification processes.Then he went around to local {ponds} and streams and {brought} back some plants and animals.He placed them in the tanks and waited.Little by little, these different kinds of life got {used} to one another and formed their own {ecosystem} .Much like a {symphony} , these {organisms} interact in harmony.After a few weeks, John added the sludge.
paragraphs.cn: 约翰为 <u> 他自己 </u> 设定的任务是从一些污泥中去除有害 <u> 物质 </u> 。首先，他 <u> 构建 </u> 了一个简单的 <u> 框架 </u> ，用于组织一系列相互连接的透明玻璃纤维 <u> 水箱 </u> 。每个水箱都充当一个小型生态系统，是大自然自身净化过程的 <u> 媒介 </u> 。然后，他前往当地的 <u> 池塘 </u> 和溪流周边， <u> 带回 </u> 了一些动植物，把它们放进水箱里，然后等待。渐渐地，这些不同种类的生物开始相互 <u> 适应 </u> ，形成了自己的 <u> 生态系统 </u> 。这些生物就像一部 <u> 交响乐 </u> ，和谐地互动着。几周后，约翰把污泥加了进去。

paragraphs.en: He was {amazed} at the results.The plants and animals in the eco-machine took the sludge as food and began to eat it! These living filters work tirelessly to clean the water, requiring minimal human {intervention} .Within weeks, the sludge had all been {digested} , and all that was left was {pure} {water} .Since then, he has had {faith} in nature's ability to heal when provided with the right tools.
paragraphs.cn: 结果令他感到 <u> 惊讶 </u> 。生态机器中的动植物把污泥当作食物，开始吞食它！这些有生命的过滤器不知疲倦地净化着水，几乎不需要人工 <u> 干预 </u> 。几周内，污泥就被全部 <u> 消化 </u> 了，只剩下 <u> 纯净的水 </u> 。从那以后，他就 <u> 坚信 </u> ，只要提供了合适的工具，大自然就有自我修复的能力。

paragraphs.en: Over the years John has taken on many big jobs.He developed a greenhouse-like {facility} that treated sewage ( (污水) ) from 1,600 homes in the South.He also designed a {patent} eco-machine to clean {canal} water in Fuzhou, a city in {southeast} {China} .
paragraphs.cn: 多年来，约翰承担了许多重大工作。他开发了一个类似温室的 <u> 设施 </u> ，用于处理南方1600户家庭的污水。他还设计了一种 <u> 专利 </u> 生态机器，用于清洁 <u> 中国东南部 </u> 城市福州的 <u> 运河 </u> 水。

paragraphs.en: As we face increasing water challenges in the 21st century, John's eco-machines stand as a testament to the healing power of nature, proving that the answers we seek may already be {beneath} our feet.“ {Ecological} design” is the name John gives to what he does.“Life on {Earth} is like a {box} of spare parts for the {inventor} ,”he says.“You put organisms in new relationships and observe what happens.”
paragraphs.cn: 在21世纪，当我们面临着日益严峻的水资源挑战时，约翰的生态机器就是大自然治愈力量的见证，表明我们寻求的答案可能早已在我们脚 <u> 下 </u> 。约翰将自己所做的工作称为“ <u> 生态 </u> 设计”。他说：“ <u> 地球 </u> 上的生命就像 <u> 发明家 </u> 手中的一 <u> 盒 </u> 备用零件。你将 <u> 生物 </u> 置于新的关系之中，然后观察会发生什么。” 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
